conditions: references in this Regulation to the AI Office

norms.object: references to national competent authorities or market surveillance authorities in this Regulation as references to the European Data Protection Supervisor
conditions: as regards AI systems put into service or used by Union institutions, agencies, offices and bodies

judge_runs.rationale: This is a definitional provision ('AI Office means...'), not an operative obligation. The phrase 'shall be construed as references to the Commission' is an interpretive definitional clause, not a deontic duty imposed on any actor; the candidate correctly finds no actor ('unspecified_needs_review'), which confirms there is no obligated party. Treating a definition/interpretation rule as an 'obligation' misclassifies non-operative definitional material as a binding norm, failing the deontic-type and normative-relevance checks.

This source is a definitional provision ('national competent authority means...'). Although the text uses 'shall be construed as', this is an interpretive construal rule for the meaning of a defined term, not a genuine operational obligation imposed on any actor. The candidate treats a definition/interpretive clause as a binding conduct norm, with actor 'unspecified_needs_review' because no actor is named — precisely because none is contemplated. Definitions do not create obligations for engineering teams; the 'action' ('be construed as') and 'object' are legal-interpretation artifacts, not actionable duties. This fails the binding-obligation grounding check (normative relevance) and provides no operational utility as a norm.
